# Recorded Claude output

Each file is Claude Code 2.1.332's stdout, recorded live on haiku with `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --permission-prompt-tool stdio --setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config` in a throwaway git repo, with `{"model":"haiku"}` in `.claude/settings.local.json`. The working folder is replaced with `/tmp/rec`. The `account`, `pid` and `user_output_styles_dir` of the initialize reply and the `memory_paths` and `messaging_socket_path` of `system/init` are removed. Only `initialize.jsonl` keeps the initialize reply.

- `initialize.jsonl`: an `initialize` control request, then "Reply with the single word: ok". The `control_response` lists `commands` (`name`, `description`, `argumentHint`, and `builtin`, `aliases` on some); the project skill `greet` is first. `system/init` lists the same names under `slash_commands` and the skills under `skills`.
- `question.jsonl`: "Use the AskUserQuestion tool to ask me which colour I like, options red and blue." The `can_use_tool` request for `AskUserQuestion` was answered with `allow` and `updatedInput` set to the questions plus `"answers":{"Which colour do you like?":"red"}`; the tool result and the reply ("You picked red.") show Claude read it.
- `queued.jsonl`: `--permission-mode bypassPermissions --replay-user-messages`. A user line with uuid `1111…` asks for three slow Bash steps; 2 s in, a user line with uuid `2222…` says "Also end your final reply with the word BANANA." It joins the running turn after the first tool result: a `user` line with `isReplay: true` and uuid `2222…` marks the moment, `command_lifecycle` frames mark `queued`, `started` and `completed`, and the one `result` ends with BANANA.
- `fork.jsonl`: `--resume <session> --fork-session --resume-session-at <uuid>`, where the session had two turns ("My first message is the word APPLE." and "My second message is the word ZEBRA.") and the uuid is turn 1's assistant line. Asked for both words, Claude answers `first=APPLE second=NONE`, and `system/init` has a new session id.
